name: Strife
label: Victory Records
lede: Strife started in Thousand Oaks as a straight edge band, got Chino Moreno, Dino Cazares and Igor Cavalera onto its second album, split two years later, and came back in 2001 no longer edge.

eras.title: Straight edge, Ventura County style
eras.text: Strife formed in Thousand Oaks in 1991, northwest of Los Angeles. Two records on New Age Records and a track on a Victory Records compilation came before the first album.

years.h: Strife forms in Thousand Oaks, California
years.p: Singer Rick Rodney and guitarist Andrew Kline start a straight edge hardcore band northwest of Los Angeles.

years.h: My Fire Burns On... is Strife's first record, on New Age Records
years.p: The 7" comes out on the Southern California straight edge label. A self-titled release follows the same year.

years.h: Strife lands What Will Remain? on Victory's Only the Strong
years.p: Victory Records' 1993 compilation, catalog VR10, also has [[Snapcase|90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd]].

eras.title: One Truth, then the road
eras.text: One Truth put a Southern California straight edge band on Chicago's Victory Records. Strife toured it, filmed it, and shared a live record with labelmates from Syracuse and Buffalo.

years.src: Wikipedia: Strife · AllMusic · No Echo: Strife In This Defiance
years.h: One Truth becomes Victory Records catalog number 14
years.p: Strife's debut LP. AllMusic's Greg Prato calls the band the one that led California hardcore's charge in the early-to-mid 90s.
years.xp:
The label credit depends on who you ask. AllMusic's bio says the album came out through Caroline Records before Strife signed to Victory; Wikipedia lists it as a Victory release from the start.

It cost about $7,500 to make, against roughly $30,000 for In This Defiance three years later. Victory reissued it in 2006.

years.cap: Igor Cavalera drums with Strife on the Roots tour, 1996
years.src: AllMusic · No Echo: Strife Witness a Rebirth
years.h: Strife films a home video of life on the road
years.p: One Truth Live shows what touring hardcore in the 90s looked like, warts and all, according to AllMusic. The Grey single comes out the same year.
years.xp: Strife spent part of 1996 on the Roots tour with Sepultura. Cavalera, who would drum on In This Defiance a year later, remembered how they met: "I saw Strife playing in Phoenix...I really loved the show, and we bonded."

years.cap: Strife with Sepultura on the Roots tour, 1996
years.h: California Takeover Live puts three bands on one record
years.p: Victory Records catalog 042 has Strife's To an End and Lift next to [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]] and [[Snapcase|90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd]].

eras.title: The record with the guests
eras.text: For its second album Strife had Chino Moreno, Dino Cazares and Igor Cavalera sit in. The band split two years later, and Victory cleaned out the vault.

years.cap: Gang vocals at Sound City, Van Nuys, with Dino Cazares of Fear Factory, 1997
years.src: Wikipedia: In This Defiance · AllMusic · No Echo: Strife In This Defiance
years.h: Chino Moreno, Dino Cazares and Igor Cavalera show up for In This Defiance
years.p: Deftones' Chino Moreno sings on Will to Die, Fear Factory's Dino Cazares adds guitar, and Sepultura's Igor Cavalera plays extra drums. AllMusic says Strife finally hit everything just right.
years.xp:
Rick Rodney, Andrew Kline and Todd Turnham played guitars and vocals, Chad Peterson bass and Sid Niesen drums. The band recorded at Sound City in Van Nuys, right after a month on tour with Sepultura, and Bob Marlette mixed it. "It sounds like it does because we had it mixed by Bob Marlette," Rodney said.

Metal Hammer later ranked it seventh among the most underrated hardcore albums, and a Canadian straight edge band took its name from the record. Strife played it front to back at select shows in 2018.

years.p: The song from In This Defiance also lands on the Hopeless Records sampler Cinema Beer Nuts.

years.cap: Strife at Sound City, Van Nuys
years.h: Strife breaks up over creative differences and exhaustion
years.p: Two years after In This Defiance, just as things seemed to be going well, according to AllMusic.
years.xp: The date is soft. AllMusic dates the breakup to early 1998; Wikipedia places it two years after the 1997 album. Either way, it came right after the band's best-received record.

years.h: Truth Through Defiance collects live tracks and rarities
years.p: Victory Records (VR092) releases it after Strife has already split, mixing live recordings with unreleased material.

eras.title: Back, and no longer edge
eras.text: Benefit shows brought Strife back, and within a year it was a band again. The comeback record dropped straight edge but kept the anger.

years.p: Strife plays several benefit concerts, a year or so after breaking up.

years.h: Strife returns with Angermeans and drops straight edge
years.p: AllMusic's verdict, in full: a kick in the butt for a whole hardcore movement. Recorded at The Steakhouse in North Hollywood for Victory Records.
years.xp:
Kline called it "a more mature and focused continuation" of In This Defiance. The lyrics are Rodney's, most of the music Kline's. The Daily Herald found it "vicious," with "as much Slayer as Agnostic Front in its lineage." Rock Hard gave it 8.5 out of 10.

The album was followed by Strife's first major tour in nearly four years.

eras.title: Brazil, with Terror's drummer
eras.text: Victory reissued the catalog, and Strife kept touring far from Thousand Oaks: Japan, South America, Europe, Mexico. The next record, 11 years after the last, was produced by Terror's drummer and mixed in São Paulo.

years.h: Victory reissues One Truth, In This Defiance and Angermeans
years.p: All three Strife albums go back in print, five years after the last new one.

years.cap: Chad Peterson at the Cobalt Cafe, Canoga Park, 2011
years.src: Wikipedia: Strife · No Echo: Strife Witness a Rebirth
years.h: Strife and Floorpunch tour Japan together
years.p: East Coast youth crew band [[Floorpunch|8ecf80c2-d090-4cbd-97ec-0a0824301041]] joins a run that also takes Strife through South America, Europe and Mexico.
years.xp: South America left an impression. "The kids there were just so appreciative for the bands traveling to their country," Kline said.

years.cap: Nick Jett and Andrew Kline at the Witness a Rebirth sessions
years.src: Wikipedia: Witness a Rebirth · No Echo: Strife Witness a Rebirth
years.h: Terror's Nick Jett produces Witness a Rebirth
years.p: Strife's first album in 11 years is out on 6131 and Holy Roar. [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]] drummer Nick Jett produces and drums, Igor Cavalera and Marc Rizzo guest, and it's mixed at Nova Studios in São Paulo.
years.xp:
Kline told No Echo: "We wanted this record to sound like what the follow up to 'In This Defiance' should have sounded like." He said he joked to Cavalera that he could play drums, and "Iggor said he was down." Members of Terror contributed too.

Chad Peterson: "This was the smoothest recording process I've ever been a part of." AllMusic and Louder both gave the record 2.5 stars out of 5.

eras.title: Andrew Kline's side roads
eras.text: Strife's guitarist kept one foot in the band and started other things: a group with Terror's singer, and his own label, which put In This Defiance back on vinyl.

years.h: Kline and Terror's Scott Vogel start World Be Free
years.p: Kline teams with [[Scott Vogel|4ab1b4fb-f2fe-458c-a496-0de55c7bf3cb]], Sammy Siegler, Joe Garlipp and Alex Barreto, later on Revelation Records. Strife plays on too: hate5six filmed a full set that November.

years.h: Kline's WAR Records presses 100 copies of In This Defiance
years.p: His own label puts the 1997 album on vinyl. Victory reissues it again in 2020.

years.h: Strife, Earth Crisis and Snapcase share a record again
years.p: The Return of the California Takeover comes 25 years after the original.
